triggers: a kernel on NVIDIA Blackwell GeForce/workstation (RTX PRO 5000 / SM120) risks the '2. CUTLASS-style SF layout is 8× bloated by default' trap

payload.goal: Avoid a known trap on NVIDIA Blackwell GeForce/workstation (RTX PRO 5000 / SM120): 2. CUTLASS-style SF layout is 8× bloated by default

problem.statement: cute-DSL NVFP4 GEMM pitfalls (sm_120, RTX PRO 5000) -- 2. CUTLASS-style SF layout is 8× bloated by default

payload.attempted: You read CUTLASS's reference `(128, 4)`-bytes-per-atom SF layout, copy it faithfully, and budget your smem accordingly. Then BLOCK_K=128 doesn't fit.
payload.lesson: Use a tight pack `(M_blocks_outer, SF_TILES_K, atoms_per_block, atom_dim, 4)` with read index `sSFA_u32[stage, kb, atom, sfa_logical, 0]` (NO `* 4`). 8× smem reduction, frees BLOCK_K=128 + STAGES=4 to fit in 100 KB. See `pack_sf_per_block` in sm120_nvfp4_pack_helpers.py. This single change accounts for **+37%** end-to-end perf (v38 → v43).

established_fact.mechanism: The (128, 4) layout matches a CUTLASS/MMA broadcast pattern where consecutive groups of 4 rows correspond to one logical SF value (so a single ldmatrix-style copy slices `sfa_phys = sfa_logical * 4`). When you instead read the SF as a single `ld.shared.u32`, only one of the four rows is touched.

payload.observed: Every stage of SF takes 512 bytes per atom, of which only **64 bytes carry data** — every 4th row holds a 4-byte SF entry (the lane-mapping `sfa_phys = sfa_logical * 4`), the other 3 rows are zero padding. With STAGES * (ATOMS_M + ATOMS_N) atoms per CTA, that's ~21 KB of zeros taking up smem you need for BLOCK_K=128 + STAGES≥3.
payload.root_cause: The (128, 4) layout matches a CUTLASS/MMA broadcast pattern where consecutive groups of 4 rows correspond to one logical SF value (so a single ldmatrix-style copy slices `sfa_phys = sfa_logical * 4`). When you instead read the SF as a single `ld.shared.u32`, only one of the four rows is touched.
